title: Canonical derived counit on a single-object augmentation
statement: Let L:C→D be an exact additive left adjoint of an additive R, with the derived-category, K-injective and functorial flat-resolution hypotheses required by the canonical derived adjunction. Transport its left adjoint through the canonical leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Then L_D of the canonical single-object right-derived augmentation, followed by the transported counit, is the exact-left single comparison followed by the single of the ordinary counit. If R is exact, transporting the right adjoint too replaces the augmentation by inverse to its termwise single comparison.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and compatibility of the Hom bijections with composition and localization.

proof.text: The defining derivedε factorization computes the counit after the right-derived unit. Naturality of the exact-left-derived identification transports this to the ordinary counit on homotopy categories, hence on complexes. Precompose by the inverse single-map comparison; check the resulting chain equality in degree zero and use that its source is zero elsewhere. For exact R the right-derived uniqueness factorization identifies augmentation followed by the exact-right-derived comparison with inverse to the single comparison. Cancel the two right-derived comparisons in the transported counit.
